$comment: One shard of the signal-lens catalogue. DATA, never loaded whole into an agent context. Validate with: python3 scripts/validate_catalogue.py

signals.name: Identity verification step reached
signals.definition: The subject enters a step that exists only to prove who they are before a transaction can complete - starting or completing a know-your-customer, age-assurance or eligibility check, submitting an identity document, or sitting in a manual review queue. Qualifying condition: a verification case keyed to a specific pending transaction or account opening reaches a recorded state (started, referred, passed, failed, abandoned). The signal is the STATE OF THE CASE. The documents, images, biometric templates and any attribute extracted from them are never signal fields - see restricted.biometric_attribute_inference.
signals.question_answered: Has this buyer cleared the last identity barrier standing between them and a completed transaction, and if not, exactly where did they stop?

capability_ladder.how: Emit one state-change event per verification case from the flow you already run - started, referred, passed, failed, abandoned - carrying the case id, the state and the transaction it blocks, and nothing else
requires: read access to the verification system's existing state changes or webhooks
capability_ladder.gives: The whole signal from data that already exists. Almost every verification flow already writes these states; they are simply visible only to the risk team and never joined to the transaction

capability_ladder.how: Record the step at which an abandoned verification stopped - document capture, selfie or liveness, address entry, wait for manual review
requires: step-level state in the verification flow
capability_ladder.gives: The difference between a fraud signal and a usability defect, which the pass/fail outcome alone hides completely

capability_ladder.how: Measure time-in-queue for manual review and alert on it, treating the queue as a revenue path rather than a compliance backlog
requires: queue timestamps, which the review tool already has
capability_ladder.gives: The highest-readiness population you have - buyers who have passed everything except your own service level - and it needs no volume to be actionable

capability_ladder.how: Join case state to the value of the transaction it blocks so recovery effort is prioritised by exposed revenue instead of queue order
requires: a shared transaction or application id between the verification system and the order or application store
capability_ladder.gives: Prioritisation, and a measured cost of your own verification friction

min_data.note: Abandonment-by-step rates are unstable below roughly 200 cases per step. The manual-review service-level signal at rung 3 is usable from day one and needs no volume at all.

access_conditions: Verification records are held for a regulatory purpose - anti-money-laundering, age assurance, sanctions screening - whose permitted uses are specified exhaustively. Using the case STATE to help the buyer complete the transaction they started is inside that purpose; exporting it into an advertising audience is a separate decision with a separate basis, and in several regimes there is no basis available
Never copy the document image, the biometric template, the document number, or any attribute read off a document into the analytics record. Carry the state, the step and the timestamps

The verification store may lawfully contain biometric and special-category data. This row does not, and that is the reason the row carries only the state - do not close the gap by joining the analytics copy back to the source record
Retention for the verification record is set by the regulation, not by your analytics policy. A warehouse copy inherits the wrong retention clock and outlives its own lawful basis
signals.terms_note: Verification providers' processing agreements normally enumerate permitted purposes exhaustively and prohibit secondary use; the underlying anti-money-laundering and age-assurance rules impose their own purpose and retention limits independent of the contract.

freshness.note: The signal expires with the transaction it blocks, or when the verification is re-run. A verification state with no live transaction behind it is a compliance record, not an intent signal, and must not be scored as one.

false_positives: Verification run for account recovery, a password reset, or a periodic re-verification of an existing customer - no new purchase behind it
A regulated re-screening cycle (sanctions, politically-exposed-person, annual refresh) the customer did not initiate
An age check triggered by content access rather than by a purchase
Fraud and account-farm operators completing verification at scale: high completion rates, zero purchase intent
A person verifying on behalf of a company, a client or a dependant they represent
Sandbox or QA cases leaking into production reporting
An abandonment caused by a broken document-capture step on one device or browser, which reads as a risk signal but is a defect in your own flow

evidence.note: Author judgement: submitting identity documents is a high-effort, low-ambiguity act that people do not perform speculatively. Not measured.
Author judgement. The record is authoritative and machine-generated with no self-report in it; the residual doubt is population contamination (re-verification, fraud rings), not measurement error.

signals.name: Payment method preparation
signals.definition: The subject puts a means of payment in place at or before the point of purchase - attaching, updating or re-authorising a payment instrument, completing a wallet or bank-authorisation handshake, passing a zero-value verification authorisation, or selecting a payment method at checkout. Qualifying condition: a tokenised payment instrument is created, updated, or authorised (successfully or not) against the subject or account. The fields are the token reference and the state; primary account numbers, security codes and bank credentials are never signal fields and must not leave the payment environment.
signals.question_answered: Can this buyer actually pay us right now - and if they tried, did it succeed, and if not, why?

capability_ladder.how: Subscribe to the payment-instrument events your payment platform already emits - instrument attached, instrument updated, authorisation succeeded, authorisation failed - and store the token reference, the method class and the state
requires: an existing merchant account and its webhook or events API
capability_ladder.gives: The signal from data you are already being sent. In most companies these events reach finance and stop there

capability_ladder.how: Split declines by reason class - insufficient funds, expired instrument, issuer decline, strong-authentication abandoned
requires: the decline reason your platform already returns, mapped to a small class list
capability_ladder.gives: The single most valuable distinction in this row: an abandoned authentication step is a recoverable readiness signal with a usability cause, an issuer decline is not

capability_ladder.how: Add a zero-value or account-verification authorisation when an instrument is attached, so 'they added a card' becomes 'they added a card that works'
capability_ladder.gives: Removes the largest false positive in this row - instruments that are attached but not chargeable

capability_ladder.how: Join instrument state to the order attempt so 'ready to pay and did not' is separated from 'tried to pay and could not'
requires: a shared order or checkout-session id
capability_ladder.gives: Two populations that need opposite treatments - an objection to answer versus a failure to recover

min_data.note: Decline-reason mix varies sharply by issuer, method and country. Below roughly 500 attempts a decline-class breakdown is not stable enough to route on, though the individual events are actionable one at a time from day one.

access_conditions: Card data is in scope for the payment card industry's security standard. The catalogue's fields are a token reference and a state; a primary account number, security code, full track data or a bank credential must never enter an analytics store, a CRM or an audience. Pulling card numbers into a warehouse to build this signal extends your compliance scope to the warehouse

Bank-authorisation style connections are consented for a stated purpose and a stated period. That consent does not extend to marketing segmentation and it expires - the connection lapsing is not a signal about the buyer

Merchant and processor agreements generally permit use of your own transaction data but restrict onward transfer and re-identification; check before joining instrument data to any third-party audience

Do not build this signal client-side by observing card-field interactions. That is both a card-security scope problem and the pattern behavioural-telemetry claims target, and it is unnecessary - every rung above is server-side
signals.terms_note: Access is governed by your merchant or processor agreement, which defines permitted use of transaction data and normally prohibits onward transfer and re-identification; the card-security standard separately constrains where card data may be stored at all.

freshness.note: An authorisation hold and a checkout session both expire on the payment platform's clock, typically within days. After that the buyer has to start again and the signal is spent, not merely weaker.

false_positives: A card updated on an existing subscription - a retention event, not new demand
An instrument added to start a free trial where no charge is imminent
Card testing and enumeration attacks, which generate large volumes of attach and decline events with no buyer behind them at all
A finance or procurement user loading a corporate card for somebody else's purchase
A wallet auto-fill that attaches an instrument without a deliberate decision by the person
An authorisation retried by your own dunning system rather than initiated by the customer
Internal or QA transactions run against a live merchant account

evidence.note: Author judgement: presenting a means of payment is the last act before money moves. Not measured.

Author judgement. The event is machine-generated and unambiguous, but card-testing traffic can dominate raw volumes, which is why rung 3's verification authorisation matters more here than the score does.

signals.name: Billing account setup
signals.definition: The subject configures the commercial plumbing the purchase will run through - creating or completing a billing profile, entering a billing or tax address, a tax registration number, a purchase-order or cost-centre reference, an invoicing contact, or requesting invoice-based payment terms. Qualifying condition: at least one billing-only field, one that exists solely in order to invoice somebody, is completed against an account. A shipping address or a login profile is not this signal.
signals.question_answered: Has somebody started doing the administrative work that only happens once a purchase has been decided internally?

capability_ladder.how: Flag the account the first time any billing-only field is completed - tax number, billing address, invoicing contact, purchase-order reference - and store that first-completion timestamp
requires: read access to the billing or commerce records you already hold
capability_ladder.gives: A decision-taken flag from fields that already exist. The fields are always there; the first-completion timestamp almost never is, and it is the part that carries the signal

capability_ladder.how: Separate 'the user completed it' from 'a different person completed it' by comparing the completing subject to the account's active users
requires: a user id on the billing edit
capability_ladder.gives: A finance or procurement contact appearing on the billing profile is a buying group forming, and it is one comparison away

capability_ladder.how: Detect the procurement-shaped variants explicitly: a purchase-order reference, a request for invoicing terms instead of card payment, a supplier-onboarding form, a tax-certificate or vendor-questionnaire request
requires: routing those inbound requests into a structured field rather than an inbox
capability_ladder.gives: The strongest variants in this row - each is a step nobody takes speculatively

capability_ladder.how: Join first-billing-field completion to the eventual order date and learn your own lag from billing setup to purchase
requires: order records joined on account id
capability_ladder.gives: A follow-up window measured on your own business rather than a generic one, which is what this signal is actually for

min_data.note: The billing-setup-to-order lag at rung 4 needs roughly 100 completed orders before the median stops moving. The boolean flag at rung 1 is usable immediately and at any volume.

access_conditions: Tax registration numbers and legal entity names are business identifiers, but a sole trader's tax number can be a personal identifier in some jurisdictions. Store and score the field CLASS - 'a tax number is present' - rather than the value

Billing records carry statutory retention periods longer than most marketing retention policies. Copying them into a marketing store imports the wrong retention clock and creates data you cannot delete on request but also should not be holding for that purpose

In a reseller or agency motion the billing account and the deciding organisation are different entities; treat the billing account as the identity this signal attaches to and do not infer the end customer's readiness from it

freshness.note: Billing setup is close to the decision but not to the moment: in a business motion the gap between a completed billing profile and a first invoice runs to weeks. Measure your own lag at rung 4 and use it in place of this default.

false_positives: A finance team completing billing details for an unrelated existing contract or a renewal
Vendor onboarding completed for a procurement or security compliance review with no purchase attached to it
A tax, address or entity-name correction on an established account
Billing details entered only to unlock a free tier or trial that requires a card or a tax number
An agency or reseller setting up billing on behalf of a client whose decision is not made
A duplicate account created by an organisation that already buys from you, inflating account-level counts
Staff testing the billing flow with real details in a production account

evidence.note: Author judgement: billing administration is unpleasant work that people only do once the buying decision has been made internally. Not measured.
Author judgement, held at 4 because free tiers and trials that demand billing details for anti-abuse reasons manufacture this event on accounts that never intended to buy.

signals.name: Account and access verification
signals.definition: The subject removes the account-level barriers that stand before a transaction - verifying an email address or phone number, completing domain or workspace verification, configuring single sign-on, enrolling in multi-factor authentication, accepting an invitation to an existing account, or receiving administrator approval. Qualifying condition: an account state transition from unverified to verified, or from single-member to multi-member, is recorded. This is account hygiene, not identity proofing; for regulated identity checks see f08.identity_verification.
signals.question_answered: Has this account moved from a casual sign-up to something an organisation is standing behind - and has a second person joined it?

capability_ladder.how: Timestamp the verification transitions your own authentication system already performs - email verified, phone verified, invitation accepted - onto the account record instead of leaving them in an auth log nobody queries
requires: read access to your own auth events
capability_ladder.gives: The signal today, from events you already generate, with no new collection from the user

capability_ladder.how: Classify the verified email domain as corporate, free-mail or disposable using a list you maintain yourself
requires: a domain list you own and update
capability_ladder.gives: The cheapest business qualification signal that exists on a self-serve account - and it needs no vendor, no enrichment purchase and no third-party lookup

capability_ladder.how: Count distinct verified members per account and the lag between the first and the second
capability_ladder.gives: The moment a single user becomes a buying group. This is the most under-used field in the family and it is already in your database

capability_ladder.how: Treat single sign-on configuration, domain verification or an administrator approval step as a separate and stronger state than personal verification
capability_ladder.gives: Authority arriving as an observed event rather than an inference: somebody with organisational standing had to act for it to happen

min_data.note: A 'second verified member within N days' rule needs roughly 200 accounts with 90 days of history before N can be tuned to anything. The individual state transitions are usable at any volume.

access_conditions: Authentication logs are security records. Give the analytics copy its own minimal schema - account, subject, transition, timestamp - rather than replicating the log, which carries IP addresses and device data you do not need for this signal and should not retain for this purpose

Where the account belongs to a customer organisation, seat, role and membership data is governed by your contract with that organisation as well as by privacy law; a customer's employee list is not yours to enrich

Free-mail and disposable-domain classification must be maintained as your own list. Buying it re-introduces a third-party dependency for a judgement you can make yourself, and vendor domain lists go stale in exactly the way this catalogue avoids naming vendors to prevent

This row resolves a natural person from your own records. Even where the data is first-party and the processing is expected, a transparency duty attaches; where any field arrives from a source other than the individual, GDPR Art 14 notice is owed.

freshness.note: The verified state is a persistent fact; the intent lives in the transition. A verification six months old describes the account, not this week's demand - which is why the required fields are the transition and its timestamp rather than the current state.

false_positives: Verification completed only to use a free tier or to open gated content
A corporate email address on a personal evaluation account with no organisational sponsorship behind it
A second verified member who is a colleague invited for a look rather than a stakeholder in a decision
Bulk invitations generated by a referral incentive or a growth loop rather than by a buying process
Multi-factor enrolment enforced by workspace policy, not chosen by the user - a policy artefact that reads as commitment
Re-verification after a security incident, a device change or a password reset
Contractors, agencies and support staff verified into a customer's account, inflating the member count without adding a buyer

evidence.note: Author judgement, deliberately the lowest in this family. Email verification is table stakes for using anything; the strength lives almost entirely in rungs 3 and 4 - a second verified member, or domain and single sign-on configuration - not in the base transition. Not measured.
Author judgement. The events themselves are exact and system-generated; what they imply about intent is weak, which is the reason strength and reliability diverge on this row.
